Ensure the `libvirt` GROUP exists before any libvirt package is configured.
On Ubuntu 26.04 (resolute), libvirt-daemon-system's maintainer script adds the
libvirt-qemu user to the `libvirt` group BEFORE it creates that group, so dpkg
writes `fatal: The group \`libvirt' does not exist.` into the package log. The
group exists moments later and the install succeeds, but charly's deploy log
gate rightly refuses to ignore a `fatal:` line, so a 26.04 VM bed cannot pass.
Measured, both directions: with the group pre-created the same install emits
ZERO such lines; reordering the packages does not help (the message simply
moves to whichever transaction configures libvirt-daemon-system).
This candy exists to be `require:`-ordered AHEAD of `virtualization`, because
charly emits a candy's declarative distro: packages before its plan: steps - a
plan step inside virtualization would run too late. Idempotent and harmless on
Fedora/Arch, where the group already exists or the check simply passes.
opencharly/distro-ubuntu#66.

## Acceptance plan

This candy's `plan:` — the runnable spec `charly check` executes against a live deployment. `check:` steps are idempotent probes; `run:` steps change state.

| Intent | Step |
|---|---|
| `run` | ensure the libvirt group exists |
| `check` | the libvirt group exists, which is what libvirt-daemon-system's postinst expects |
